The password security practice described in the text is highly insecure. Using the same password for every account creates a single point of failure; if one account is compromised, all other accounts using that same password are immediately vulnerable. While changing the password monthly might mitigate the window of opportunity for an attacker who has obtained the password, it does not address the fundamental risk of credential stuffing or data breaches across multiple services. A stronger practice would be to use a unique, complex password for each account, ideally managed with a password manager.

A group of crows is called a murder.
